response.rationale: R1 captures the core MIS-C syndrome (fever, abdominal pain, rash, conjunctivitis) and the epidemiological context of COVID-19 exposure; negative PCR is expected in post-infectious MIS-C. R3 has classic mucocutaneous findings but lacks abdominal pain and the COVID link, making MIS-C more likely.

rejected.why: sJIA lacks mucocutaneous findings and has no COVID-19 exposure context.
Infectious mononucleosis does not explain the rash, conjunctivitis, or strawberry tongue.
Redundant completion of R1; adds only the COVID exposure context already present in the vignette.
